artists.biography:
Steven John Wilson (born 3 November 1967) is an English musician, best known as the founder, lead guitarist, singer and songwriter of progressive rock band Porcupine Tree. He is involved in many other bands and musical projects both as musician and producer (including No-Man and Blackfield) and also maintains a solo career.
Wilson is a self-taught producer, audio engineer, guitar and keyboard player, playing other instruments as and where required (including bass guitar, concert harp, hammered dulcimer and flute).
He used to split his living time between Tel Aviv and London, England, but he no longer holds a permanent residence in Tel Aviv.

perplexity.description:
Harmonic Divergence (The Harmony Codex Remixed And Reimagined)" is a remix album by Steven Wilson, released in 2024 as a special vinyl-only edition for Record Store Day. It features reinterpretations of tracks from Wilson's seventh studio album, The Harmony Codex (2023), blending electronic and rock elements through diverse remix styles. Notable contributors include Ewan Pearson, who delivers a euphoric, propulsive remix of "Time Is Running Out," and Mogwai, who provides a darker, layered reinterpretation of the title track. The album showcases a range of approaches, from extended remixes to shorter thematic interludes, highlighting the original's genre-spanning complexity in a new light.

This release occupies a unique place in Wilson's discography as a companion to The Harmony Codex, emphasizing the electronic textures and experimental rock foundations of the original material through collaborative reinterpretation. While The Harmony Codex was praised for its intricate, puzzle-like musical structure, Harmonic Divergence expands on this by inviting other artists to reimagine the work, thus broadening its sonic palette. The album was issued by Virgin Music Group and SW Records, reflecting Wilson's continued exploration of blending progressive rock with electronic music influences.

Commercially and critically, Harmonic Divergence serves more as a collector’s and fan-focused project rather than a mainstream release, with its limited vinyl format and Record Store Day exclusivity. It complements the positive reception of The Harmony Codex by offering fresh perspectives on its tracks, though detailed critical reviews specific to this remix album are limited compared to the original studio album.
